In England, watching E-sports in a pub with people is a rare chance. so when I saw that the 'Pub Stomp' section of the DOTA2 website had entries not only for England but for Birmingham (a place only about 25 miles from where I live) I was thrilled so thrilled in fact that I booked a day off work to recover from the epic outing and arranged for a family member to look-after my daughter. Then I began planning my adventure...

I'm not an experienced DOTA2 player or even a close follower of the game as an e-sport I'm just getting into it (as a viewer) so the idea of sitting in a pub and watching it live really hooked me in. I was fired up to watch it, the concept is awesome. Even if it was a small turn out I would no doubt meet some awesome fellow gamers, watch my buddy get pretty hammered (I don't consume the booze personally) and have a pretty interesting experience as a whole. Maybe even find some serious love for watching E-Sports with other people.

So, on Saturday night my good friend and I ventured out a distance from the edge of the field in which we live into the big scary city. Hoping to have an adventure the likes of which have not been seen since the movie Adventures in Babysitting, but, you know, with DOTA2 watching and a bar.

First we confirmed the listing on the DOTA2 Pubstomp page (you know the one, the one on the DOTA 2 website, about as official as one of these things can be. In fact, let me get you a copy and paste of the actual listing..... 

Pubstomp in the Birmingham area!

Come to Cherry Red in Brum for beer and Doto, and bring a friend. We'll be watching the whole English stream for the last two days (Friday and Saturday). Come for a game, or stay the whole night! Bring friends!

Start Time: Friday, August 7, 04:00pm
End Time: Sunday, August 9, 01:00am

Cherry Reds 
India house 88-90 John Bright Street
Birmingham, Avon B14 7RZ

I now realise that I should have been suspicious when the text in the listing calls the game 'Doto' :/ - also Birmingham is not in the county of AVON but looking at the rest of the listings everything in England is either London or Avon according to the page. Lets forgive that one this once, England is a complicated place of Tea and double decker buses. Besides the listing clearly said 'Brum' so I knew it wasn't some new place that had popped up over night in Avon.

Firstly my buddy and I used the epic (and very useful) Google Maps to get to the post code 'B14 7RZ' as the listing shows using my awesome little blue car.

Sure enough there was the pub as expected - Cherry Red. We parked up (paying almost £4) at the nearest public car park we could find and walked the five minutes back to the pub. As we was running a little late (because we have Jobs and stuff) we expected the event to be in full swing.

To our shock, the pub was more of a hipster coffee house with a wine rack than old english beer hole. That was fine after all who cares, it was small and had pretty cool décor. Actually it was a really nice if tiny venue... but... alas, NO DOTA in sight!

hmmmmm a conundrum... We checked the full address... the post code led to a place in Edgbaston, Cherry Reds but the ROAD on the listing was a place slap bang in Birmingham City Centre.

We realised that time was stalking us like a hidden beast of fail and screamed with haste.... "TO THE HEX MOBILE!" with that we dashed back to my car and travelling as fast as legally enforced speed limits and common scene would allow we skilfully made it to a big red car park by a big red building (the Mailbox) in the heart of the city (not the Whitesnake album, but actually the middle of the city)

We dashed to the address - thanks again Google maps and your 'on foot' mode (also, thanks Android Wear for giving me directions on my wrist, so not making me look like a tourist - its like living in the future)

There it was! ANOTHER pub called Cherry Reds! (part of a chain that's pretending not to be a chain I would think) this one larger but still smaller than expected and again a very nice place. WHAT?!?!?! NO DOTA?

This time we knew we had the right place, we looked around. Only took us about 10 seconds, it was small, no chance we missed a screen. Again, address checked, yeah, right place this time (wrong post code and county but it was 'Cherry Reds' on the correct road) I actually had to queue for a few min's to talk to a staff member who was doing a fantastic job supplying some tasty looking hot caffeinated beverages. The conversation went something like this...

Me: Hello sir dude, is this here? (showed him my phone with listing on screen)

Dude: Yeah (looks closer)

Me: There supposed to be a DOTA2 thing happening today? (I made a statement but used the inflections of my voice to show that it was actually a query - I know, slick)

Dude: oh yeah, yeah, yeah, (might have been one or two more 'yeah' in there, it was actually like listening to Abed from the show Community) no. that was last night. . . .. . (looks at me)

Me: But the listing says Friday AND Saturday night sir dude! - well, it actually says it ends Sunday (I don't really know what I expected him to say if I'm honest, but I wanted some sort of response)

Dude: Blinks, looks at me... with his judging eyes That was last night.

Not only did I not get to watch the game live (could have sat ass down in the pub and streamed it to my phone, not what I had planned, also, that's a strange thing to do.) my buddy and I went to get a Burrito and then found a cinema that luckily had a showing of Ant Man about to start... it was still a good night because I got food and saw a movie with the words MARVEL at the start but not at all what I had planned.

In closing I would like to say that the E-Sports scene will never gain traction for pub showings if this sort of thing is normal. everything about the listing on the website was wrong.

Issues with postcode/road name.

Issues with date/day

Pub management that don't think that e-sports are important enough to get basic information right. (or cancel the second night without updating the listing - not even a sign on the door explaining why it was cancelled)

it was never made clear when it was being shown, when the actual 'event' started or when it was planned to finish, as someone just getting into e-sports its very hard to follow and this sort of outing does not enthuse me.

I can't say that I will be risking a wasted trip again, in future I'll watch my E-Sports at home and order a pizza. Its a shame really, I wanted to support the whole pubstomp concept with my hard earned money and presence.

The only way to enjoy life is to risk it. Go skydiving. Climb a mountain. Try free diving. Lift heavy things. Push yourself to the limits. Nothing like a shallow water blackout or ground rush to remind you how awesome life is.
Build something. Anything really. Make something with your own hands that you can point to and say "You see that? I made that."

The first thing you have to do is completely rethink how you were told to live. Do you know who you are? Do you know what you really want and love? I'm talking about the things you would gladly do but don't, for whatever reason. You need to understand your relationship with, and desire for those things, and embrace a careful hedonism whereinm short of what is going to really hurt you, you learn to not hold yourself back from pleasure. This doesn't necessarily mean being irresponsible or sleeping around at epic levels. It means practicing the fine art of indulging yourself on a regular basis.

Start trying out new foods and eating the occasional truly guilty meal. I'm talking about putting a package of bacon in the oven and eating it all yourself. Take up hobbies on pure whim and experiment with them. Do something utterly ridiculous that isn't going to break your legs. Travel, if you can afford it.

Evaluate your friendships and try to eliminate making chit-chat as a regular standby, if you have a tendency to do that. Bring up weird things. Ask people to try something with you, and note the people who are down for adventures. These are the guys who can turn you on to new stuff.

Try not to make commitments or take up responsibilities. Short-term is good, but watch out for long-term. Prioritize yourself. You can always say no, and change your mind, but saying yes can be a trap. Don't bite off more than you can, or want to, chew.

Spoil yourself when you can. Take a nap when you can. Eat slow meals and savor them. Stare out at nature. Space out. Throw a one-person dance party and take up the ethical version of "do it because you can." Go watch old TV shows you used to love with like friends and see if they held up. Do coloring books if you liked that. Have a smores night and build blanket forts.

Aim for long, lasting pleasures mainly, and some shorter-lived ones. A vacation is something to look forward to, but is short and expensive. Buy something that would cost the same amount, but give you many more hours of enjoyment-- unless getting away really would do that for you.

If you want to try something dangerous, make careful preparations and get the help of people you trust. Whether that's drugs or going skydiving or what. Don't do anything that will try to control you.

On that note, people who try to control you-- try eliminating them from your life. Always ask, What If? Not just, What If I Climbed A Mountain, but What If I Stopped Giving A Shit About This Dumb Thing? What If I Quit My Job? What If I Never Had To Deal With ____ Again?

For your job, and this doesn't work if you prioritize money-- which is how a lot of people would acquire the things they find fun-- find someplace that's -pleasant- to work that won't have you in the red, to a level you can tolerate. I make lousy pay, but I generally enjoy my job, and I very much love the people I work with. I'm okay with what I'm doing, and it has ups and downs. But, I never have to take my work home, it doesn't have much in the way of deadlines, I'm not micromanaged, my bosses are great people, and I'm not physically or mentally exhausting myself on a regular basis. In short, try something that isn't stressful, if you can.

Every person is different, and your needs are bound to be different from mine. But, that's my approach. It seems backwards to some people, until they talk to me long enough. If you're a very active person, replace some of this thinking nonsense with sports, even extreme sports. Try Extreme Ironing. Try something you-- even if you have to create it. Just start combining things you like.

Remember, money is imaginary. You're buying things with hours of your life and your physical health as valued by a market that couldn't care less. Purchase long-term items, and bring things into your life that don't really cost, like friends who help you grow.

Last, but not least-- if none of this works for you, and you're instead crippled by ennui and depression, congratulations/condolences: you are looking for meaning in your life, which cannot be bought or traveled to, maybe can't be solved. But, you can decide if and how you think it exists. Objective meaning and purpose may not exist for you. Subjective meaning and purpose may not come into existence for you. If you get to this point, just start reading a ton of philosophy... or learn to give up the quest and embrace being able to ask a question without needing to know the answer, maybe.
